answer:
Hook the `editor:complete` event. Register your handler with `event.listen`, for example `event.listen { name = "editor:complete", run = function(e) ... end }`. The handler can return extra completion items.

The `editor:complete` event is described in `Completion.md` and `Event.md`. The `event.listen` call is documented in `API/event.md`. I didn't find an example that combines the two, so the call above is my own composition from the documented syntax.

6	SilverBullet provides context-aware autocomplete to help you write faster. Completions are triggered automatically or via keyboard shortcuts as you type.
7	
8	# Page link completion
9	Type `[[` to trigger page name completion. SilverBullet searches across all pages in your space and offers matching suggestions. Select one to insert a [[Link]] to that page. If no page with that name exists, a link is still created — navigating to it will create the page (these are tracked as [[Aspiring Pages]]).
10	
11	# Tag completion
12	Type `#` to trigger tag completion. SilverBullet suggests existing tags from across your space. This helps maintain consistent tagging — no more typos creating duplicate tags.
13	
14	# Emoji completion
15	Type `:` followed by a keyword to search for emoji. For example, `:rocket` offers the rocket emoji. Press Enter to insert it.
16	
17	# Frontmatter key completion
18	Inside a [[Frontmatter]] block, SilverBullet suggests attribute keys that are already used elsewhere in your space. This helps keep your metadata schema consistent.
19	
20	# Slash commands
21	Type `/` at the beginning of a line (or after a space) to trigger [[Slash Command]] completion. Slash commands can insert templates, perform actions, or trigger custom behavior defined in [[Space Lua]].
22	
23	# Lua code completion
24	Inside `space-lua` fenced code blocks, SilverBullet provides code completion for:
25	
26	* Global functions and variables
27	* API namespaces (`editor.`, `space.`, `index.`, etc.)
28	* Table fields and methods
29	* Function signatures and one-line documentation when the API provides metadata. Selecting a documented function reveals its complete source-backed API documentation in an adjacent information panel.
30	
31	Ctrl-click or Cmd-click a Lua-defined function to navigate to its definition.
32	
33	# Custom completions
34	You can extend the completion system by subscribing to the `editor:complete` event via [[Space Lua]]. Your handler receives the current cursor context and can return additional completion items.
35
